prs.author: Dharit13

They take different mechanisms to fix it - 2395 sends an in-band JSONRPCError for the specific pending request, 3098 raises a StreamableHTTPError and unwraps it out of anyio's ExceptionGroup. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same trigger: the SSE reconnection loop giving up after MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS with no way for the caller to learn the request will never complete. prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2395's fix resolves only the specific pending request via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, matching the existing error-injection pattern already used for POST failures elsewhere in this file, so it leaves the rest of the session/transport unaffected. 3098's approach raises StreamableHTTPError out of the task group, which propagates a fatal error to the whole transport context manager rather than the single hung request, and adds a new recursive `_unwrap_exception` helper to peel it out of ExceptionGroup nesting - a larger, riskier surface for what is otherwise the same reported hang.

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: stdio_server() creates its read/write memory object streams with buffer size 0, which can cause a handler's send() (e.g. a final response) to block until the stdout writer task is ready to receive again — surfacing when a progress notification is still being flushed. #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as configurable parameters (defaults stay 0, so callers must opt in). #2654 addresses the same root cause by hardcoding the write_stream buffer to 1, fixing the blocking-during-progress-notifications case by default with no caller changes needed. (2 PRs)

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests with the same JSON-RPC request id both get routed through `_request_streams` keyed by that id, so the second request silently overwrites the first's stream slot and their responses cross-wire (one gets the other's payload, the other hangs).

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a 400 rejection for an in-flight duplicate id, but #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key (falsely blocking a distinct id) and permits a string id of `_GET_stream` to collide with the reserved standalone-GET slot. #3221 fixes the same duplicate-id race but replaces the naive `str()` key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixes), closing both edge cases that #3063's diff leaves open.

clusters.pick_reason: #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError and hardcodes reconstruction as (self._elicitations, self.message) — any other MCPError subclass with a non-default __init__ stays unpicklable. #2478 adds a module-level _restore_mcp_error dispatcher but still special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError with an explicit `if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError` branch calling from_error/from_error_data, so each future subclass with a custom constructor needs its own branch added. #3262 defines __reduce__ once on the base MCPError using __new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ restoration, which round-trips any subclass's full instance state (including error.data) generically with no per-subclass code, and its test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix isn't limited to the one subclass the other two PRs target.

clusters.pick_reason: This is the only PR that changes OAuthContext.lock's underlying type from anyio.Lock to anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1), plus a separate flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions — fixing a task-affinity issue (anyio.Lock must be released by the same task that acquired it, but httpx can resume/close the auth-flow generator on a different task) that plain scope-narrowing doesn't address. #3252's diff only relocates the `async with self.context.lock` block so the lock is released before `yield request`, and #2858 (per its title/description) makes the same scope-narrowing change — both retain the original anyio.Lock type and so remain exposed to the cross-task release failure mode that #3243's semaphore swap eliminates.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a 400 rejection for an in-flight duplicate id, but #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key (falsely blocking a distinct id) and permits a string id of `_GET_stream` to collide with the reserved standalone-GET slot. #3221 fixes the same duplicate-id race but replaces the naive `str()` key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixes), closing both edge cases that #3063's diff leaves open.
